author: Pierre-MarieMarchio
name: .NET Clean Architecture API
description: A .NET 10 HTTP API on Clean Architecture, meant to be kept: a domain, use cases, infrastructure modules behind ports and a thin presentation layer, on EF Core with PostgreSQL, SQL Server or SQLite (for development), with architecture tests, CI and its own documentation. Local accounts, an external OpenID Connect provider or no authentication; Files, the example features and a first web app are options.

choices.description: The supplied Auth module: local accounts, JWT access and refresh tokens, its own database context.
Accounts held by an external OpenID Connect provider (Keycloak, Entra ID, Auth0...): bearer tokens validated against Authentication:External, each subject mapped to an internal owner.
No accounts: a public API. Needs --examples none and --files false, whose features belong to a caller.

auth.description: Who the API's callers are. none generates no Auth module and makes every endpoint public on purpose.

choices.description: Not an option to set: it names the refusal.

authNoneNeedsExamplesNone.description: Never set. --auth none refuses the example features, which each belong to a caller: add --examples none.

choices.description: Not an option to set: it names the refusal.

authNoneNeedsFilesFalse.description: Never set. --auth none refuses the Files module, whose files belong to a caller: add --files false.

choices.description: PostgreSQL: a schema per feature, the row's xmin as its version, advisory locks for the leases.
SQL Server: a schema per feature, a version counter the save stamps, application locks for the leases.
MySQL 8.4: a table prefix per feature, a version counter the save stamps, named locks for the leases.
SQLite, for development only: one file, a table prefix per feature, in-process leases; the API refuses to start outside Development.

database.description: The database the project runs on. A project carries that provider only; MySQL is not generated by this version of the template.

choices.description: Not an option to set: it names the refusal.

mySqlNotYetGenerated.description: Never set. This version of the template does not generate --database mysql yet: choose --database postgresql.

developmentConnectionString.description: The Default connection string of appsettings.Development.json, for the chosen database and the credentials .env.example gives it.

templateMaintenance.description: Never true in a generated project. Names the pieces that maintain the template itself - the acceptance matrix, the test-count floor, the tree-auditing gates, the changelog - so they stay in the template repository only.

templateVersion.description: The template package's version, which release-please raises, read by .template.config/TemplatePackage.csproj and recorded in a generated project's overview; its release is tagged v<version>.

files.description: Include the Files module: stored files, their storage adapters, the object-store container and the Files tables of the business context.

choices.description: TodoLists, Reminders and Notes.
Notes only: the simple example, with no domain model and no other feature to lean on.
No example feature: the modules, the mechanisms and their tests only.

examples.description: Which example features the project starts with. Reminders needs TodoLists, so they come together.

ci.description: Include the GitHub Actions workflows that build, test, scan and release the solution (ci.yml, codeql.yml, release.yml; web.yml with a web app).

sonar.description: Include the Sonar analysis: the local SonarQube compose profile, its scanner image and task, and the SonarQube Cloud workflow when --ci is true.

agentFiles.description: Include AGENTS.md, the brief for coding agents and people, and Src/Web/AGENTS.md with a web app. It is the only agent file the template writes.

choices.description: No web front end: the project stays a pure API.
One web app holding a static page, served by nginx, relaying /api to the API.
The same app as vite-react, kept under this name until the next major version.
One Angular web app in the pnpm workspace Src/Web, created by the Angular CLI (ng new).
One Vue web app in the pnpm workspace Src/Web, created by Vue's official CLI (create-vue, with TypeScript, Vue Router, Vitest and ESLint).
One React web app in the pnpm workspace Src/Web, created by Vite's official CLI (create-vite, react-ts).
One Vue web app in the pnpm workspace Src/Web, created by Vite's official CLI (create-vite, vue-ts).
One Svelte web app in the pnpm workspace Src/Web, created by Vite's official CLI (create-vite, svelte-ts).
One React web app in the pnpm workspace Src/Web, created by React Router's official CLI (create-react-router): a single-page app, or rendered on the server with --web-rendering ssr.
One Blazor WebAssembly app in Src/Web, created by dotnet new blazorwasm and calling the API through the .NET client of Src/Clients.

web.description: The first web front end, in the pnpm workspace Src/Web. More apps are added later with dotnet new cleanarch-webapp.

choices.description: Not an option to set: it names the refusal.

wasmWebNeedsAccounts.description: Never set. --web blazor-wasm calls the API's versioned routes, and --auth none publishes none: choose --auth local or external.

choices.description: A site for the API's users.
A back office for administrators; needs --auth local or external.

webAudience.description: Who the first web app is for; the framework apps shape their screens by it.

choices.description: Not an option to set: it names the refusal.

adminWebNeedsAccounts.description: Never set. --web-audience admin signs administrators in, which --auth none cannot: choose --auth local or external.

choices.description: A single-page app: a static site served by nginx.
Rendered on the server for each request, by the framework's own Node server, which keeps the session; angular and react-router only.

webRendering.description: How the first web app renders, where its generator offers both.

choices.description: Not an option to set: it names the refusal.

serverRenderingNeedsAServerStarter.description: Never set. --web-rendering ssr needs a web app whose generator renders on the server: choose --web angular or react-router, or --web-rendering spa.

webName.description: The first web app's name, in PascalCase: its folder Src/Web/apps/<name>, its service web-<name>, its port WEB_<NAME>_HOST_PORT.

choices.description: No presentation project beside the API.
A Blazor Web App with server interactivity in Src/Presentation, created by dotnet new blazor and calling the use cases in process.
An Avalonia desktop app in Src/Presentation, created by dotnet new avalonia.mvvm and calling the API through the .NET client of Src/Clients.

An MCP server in Src/Presentation, written in the shape of dotnet new mcpserver --transport remote, whose tools call the use cases in process for the caller its access key or its provider's token names. Needs --auth local or external.

presentation.description: A presentation project beside the API, created at bootstrap by its framework's own generator or written whole: a server host reaches the application layer in process, a client reaches the API through the .NET client. A project generated without one adds it later with dotnet new cleanarch-presentation.

choices.description: Not an option to set: it names the refusal.

clientPresentationNeedsAccounts.description: Never set. --presentation avalonia calls the API's versioned routes, and --auth none publishes none: choose --auth local or external.

choices.description: Not an option to set: it names the refusal.

mcpNeedsAccounts.description: Never set. --presentation mcp acts for the caller an access key or a provider's token names, and --auth none names nobody: choose --auth local or external.

accessKeys.description: True when local accounts have an MCP server to call: brings the access keys its callers present, their routes, table, tests and decision.

dotnetClient.description: True when the project holds a presentation or a web app that calls the API through the .NET client of Src/Clients. Brings the client, its tests, the api-client task and the Kiota tool.

presentationName.description: The presentation project's name, in PascalCase: its project <Project>.<name> in Src/Presentation, its service presentation-<name>, its port PRESENTATION_<NAME>_HOST_PORT. Portal when not given, Mcp for --presentation mcp.

choices.description: Not an option to set: it names the refusal.

presentationNameIsTaken.description: Never set. --presentation-name names a project the template already writes, which generation would overwrite: choose another name, such as Portal.

choices.description: The API runs the jobs on its timers, beside HTTP, each pass that must run once under a lease.
A worker in Src/Presentation runs the jobs, written from the shape of dotnet new worker; the API serves HTTP alone. Needs a server database.

jobs.description: The process that runs the background jobs: the API itself, or a worker of their own that the API leaves them to.

choices.description: Not an option to set: it names the refusal.

workerNeedsServerDatabase.description: Never set. --jobs worker runs the jobs in a second process, and a SQLite file serves one: choose --database postgresql or sqlserver, or --jobs api.

scaffoldedAtBootstrap.description: True when a folder under Src/Presentation or Src/Web/apps holds a scaffold.json, a project or an app bootstrap creates.

postActions.description: Bootstrap the project before anything else.

manualInstructions.text: In the project folder, run dotnet run Tools/Tasks.cs bootstrap and commit what it writes: the tests, verify and the stack assume it ran. It formats the usings around the project's name, writes the OpenAPI reference, restores the local tools and creates each context's initial migration. It needs the network, not Docker.

postActions.description: Bootstrap also creates what each scaffold.json describes.

manualInstructions.text: A folder under Src/Presentation or Src/Web/apps that holds a scaffold.json is a project or an app still to be created: bootstrap creates it as that file describes, and adds a .NET one with its tests to the solution.
It writes the client in Src/Clients from the OpenAPI reference with Kiota, one of the local tools.

postActions.description: Bootstrap also installs the web workspace.

manualInstructions.text: It installs Src/Web and writes its TypeScript API client, which needs Node.js and pnpm: run corepack enable once per machine.
